quotes.text: Use Terminal for collecting non-PCI data with the reader hardware interfaces.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: After swiping the card, Stripe provides a tokenized data object. Use the token to securely retrieve the cleartext track data on your back end.
The collected data is stored on Stripe’s servers for 24 hours.
Stripe doesn’t perform and isn’t responsible for the authentication of collected data or the authorization of transactions using collected data.

findings: The November 7, 2026 exact base-URL capture identifies the non-PCI reader-hardware purpose and indexes iOS, Android and React Native Markdown variants. The functional bodies of those variant routes are outside the pinned capture.

The May 1, 2026 capture supplies the private-preview request, reader and offline limitations, approved track format and merchant integration with non-PCI gift-card data. A customer swipes, the SDK returns a data token or error, and an authenticated merchant backend retrieves the cleartext using the token. Stripe stores it for 24 hours and disclaims data authentication, transaction authorization and third-party illegal conduct or fraud liability.

The source summary relates the May workflow accurately at a high level. Scope reader/preview/retention claims to May. The cancellation paragraph applies to supported readers with a smart-reader opt-out, not universally across all listed readers. The older capture only shows three SDK variants and does not establish exclusion of every other future integration.
substantive_changes: No functional delta is established by the November index. The observed publication change is SDK-specific navigation in place of an expanded in-page guide, with the same non-PCI purpose.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May's private-preview request details, supported S700/S710, WisePOS E, M2 and Chipper 2X BT readers, no offline support, numeric track-2 data with ISO sentinels and no separator, and contact route for formats outside the approved list.

Keep May's POS/customer swipe/SDK token-or-error/backend retrieval sequence, supported-reader cancellation limits and 24-hour storage with separate responsibility/third-party disclaimer. Keep November variant links labeled as routes.
conflicts: The existing summary and stripe-terminal concept use undated operational wording. November does not contain any replacement operational authority. Label the old behavior dated, and make the new index discoverable without transferring its omissions to product behavior.

The May nonmatching-format passage instructs merchants to contact Terminal with the format and BIN ranges. The summary's generic approval requirement is stronger than the quoted instruction. Avoid implying an approved custom format or a uniform device cancellation option.
unresolved_questions: The November base capture cannot resolve then-current access, limits, formats, device coverage, retention, disclaimer or Android/iOS/React Native variant differences. It does not establish that any prior claim was removed or that the underlying product changed.

findings: Keep the May full guide as the dated functional source and link November as the SDK variants index. Add the source-to-stripe-terminal reciprocal route and preserve its back-link.
conflicts: Qualify historically evidenced preview, device and operational details and narrow custom-format and customer cancellation wording to the old guide's actual instructions.
source_assessments.reason: The three verified variant links add a useful navigation route. The capture itself supplies no replacement for the May functional evidence.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/collect-data, source-stripe-terminal-collect-data should present November 7, 2026 as a Terminal non-PCI reader-hardware introduction with links to iOS, Android and React Native variants. See new raw lines 5-15. Those bytes do not establish SDK call, prerequisites, token state, backend retrieval, storage or Stripe responsibility. The May 1, 2026 full capture states private-preview access by a request including use case, reader and integration, format and applicable third-party provider. It describes S700/S710, WisePOS E, M2 and Chipper 2X BT, no offline mode and only approved numeric track-2 formatting. See old raw lines 8-30. The merchant's POS collects a customer swipe, the SDK returns a token or error, and the merchant backend retrieves cleartext non-PCI data for uses such as gift-card redemption within the documented 24-hour storage window. The capture limits default customer cancellation to supported readers and locates the opt-out on supported smart readers. Stripe disclaims authentication of collected data, authorization of transactions using it, and liability for third-party conduct or fraud. See old raw lines 36-76, old raw lines 82-119 and old raw lines 125-165. The current summary mostly represents that May flow. Where it says custom formats require approval, the actual quoted instruction is to contact the Terminal team with card format and BIN ranges.
